data.title: 4x4 Chess: Checkmate?
data.statement:
A war has shrunk down to a single tiny battlefield: a 4x4 chessboard.

On this board there is exactly one Black King and a handful of White Queens
(between 1 and 3). No other pieces exist. Standard chess rules apply for
the pieces present: a Queen attacks any square along its row, column, or
diagonal, as long as nothing blocks the way. A King can move one square in
any direction, as long as that square is on the board and not itself under
attack.

Your task: given the current position, determine whether the Black King is
in checkmate right now.

The Black King is in checkmate when both of these are true:
- It is currently in check (attacked by at least one Queen).
- It has no way out: every square it could move to is either off the
  board, attacked by a remaining Queen, or occupied by a Queen that
  another Queen is protecting (so capturing it would still leave the King
  in check).

Since Black only has a King, blocking a check is never an option, only
moving or capturing.
data.constraints:
The board is always 4x4.
There is always exactly one k on the board.
There are between 1 and 3 Q on the board, inclusive.
No characters other than '.', 'k', 'Q' appear on the board.
data.inputDescription:
The board is given as 4 lines of exactly 4 characters each.

Row 0 is the first line read, row 3 is the last line read. Within a line,
column 0 is the leftmost character and column 3 is the rightmost.

Each character is one of:
.  an empty square
k  the Black King (there is always exactly one)
Q  a White Queen (there are between 1 and 3)
data.outputDescription:
Output a single line:
CHECKMATE if the Black King is checkmated, or
NOT CHECKMATE otherwise.
